pages.text: Every computer comes with seven programs:$(li)$(thing)EDIT$(), the text editor: Ctrl+S saves, F3 opens, F5 prints.$(li)$(thing)SYSINFO$(): the disk, drive, scanner and what is wired up.$(li)$(thing)BANDPLAN$(): the $(l:radiocraft:propagation/band_plan)band plan$() as bars.$(li)$(thing)INSTALL$(): installs from floppy disks.$(li)$(thing)SETUP$(): launcher, colours, password, name, clock.$(li)$(thing)STUDY$(): $(l:radiocraft:computer/license_study)License Study$().$(li)$(thing)ABOUT$(): About RadioCraft.

Everything else comes on a $(item)Floppy Disk$(). Craft a blank one, then craft it with the part that stands for the program: a book and quill for the book editor, a book for the logbook, the band plan sheet for the frequency manager, a comparator for the radio programmer, and so on (look the disks up in your recipe book).$(br2)Use the disk on the computer or its monitor, or pick it in INSTALL, then install it. The disk is not used up. Sneak and right click the computer to eject it.

Rumour has it some disks were never sold in shops: old programs and games turn up in chests here and there, deep underground and in old libraries, on wrecks, and now and then in a village house. Hams who lived out in the country, in a little shack with an antenna on the roof, had a few too.$(br2)Programs can be removed in INSTALL with Del; their files stay on the disk.

Creative only: the $(item)All Applications Floppy$(). Use it on the computer or its monitor, or pick it in INSTALL, and every program that comes on a floppy is installed at once, except the secret ones. It never stays in the drive: the disk stays in your hand.

pages.title: LAN Relay and Redstone
pages.text: Computers joined by data wire or a microwave link form a $(thing)LAN$().$(br2)$(thing)RELAY$() is its chat room: one computer is set as a relay server (F5; it needs a name and background services on) and keeps the room.$(br2)$(thing)REDSTONE$() sets a $(item)Computer Redstone Block$() touching a computer, from there or from a computer it lets in. Name its levels: 4 can be "Door Open".

$(thing)EMAIL$() sends mail to $(thing)user@COMPUTER$() on the LAN: your username there (the one RELAY uses) and the computer's SETUP name.$(br2)A computer takes mail while someone is at it, or with its background services on. Otherwise the mail waits in the sender's outbox and goes when that computer is back; after three days it comes back undelivered.
